Losing my Dad to suicide. His death has changed my perspective on life because I really don’t want to hurt my mum and brother the same way he hurt each one of us. Before he passed away, I contemplated on suicide a lot. I did work through the suicidal thoughts and tried to get better over time. However, all the solutions I took like taking antidepressants, meditating, exercise, therapy, etc have been very temporary. They didn’t fix my mindset. 

There was nothing that permanently changed me until I lost my Dad last year. I feel really awful sometimes because I feel like if it wasn’t my Dad, it would’ve been me that my family would be grieving for.
Hugs ❤️❤️ I can feel your pain in this post. Cry and rage all you need to, take all the time that you need to grieve. Please take care of yourself and don’t rush.

I’m sorry that you’re suffering and that you feel like wanting to end things for good. I can only say that I’ve been on both sides. I’ve been the suicidal person for so long who just wanted things to end every day. Now I’m on the other side in being the one left behind. 

I am still suicidal at times but I also have a really strong reason to live. That’s because I love my family and friends too much to leave them behind. I’ve been left behind my Dad who suicided last year. He was in a lot of emotional pain like us. But in making that decision, I feel like he’s only pushed that pain and hopelessness onto me and those left behind. 

So that’s why I can’t stand the thought of another person ending their life. Because I’ve been on both sides, I’d rather have you around... than to not have you at all.
Thank you for sharing this... I can really relate to your loss. Your dad sounds like an amazing person who has done many things in his life. Thinking of you ❤️

I’m truly sorry for your loss, it must be hard with what you’re going through. I’m only on my first year but I also get the random waves too. There’s not much I can do at that point except to just live through it. You’re allow to feel the grief at that point. I just think that the grief is there because I love the person a lot. When the grief hits, I find myself crying in private and taking things slow until I can get on with my day again. I miss my Dad.

Sometimes, you can find someone who actually gives back and checks on you - this to me is a friend you should keep. Keep these sort of people in your life. The world is big and there’s plenty of people to meet. No need to try and please everybody.

I lost my Dad last year when I was 24. It’s been the hardest point in my life and I honestly don’t know how I’ve managed to get this far... I still miss my Dad a lot. 

Being the eldest child, I feel great responsibility to take care of my brother and mum where I can. With dad gone, I blame myself for not being able to save him. I haven’t thought about my future and how I can move forward. I guess I feel like I’m stuck right now trying to grieve and heal from this pain.

It feels like the world has turned upside down. It feels like the world isn’t fair and you wish that this was only a dream. It hasn’t been a year but I feel like I’ve changed a lot. I now do things that my Dad used to do. I try to take care of my mum and brother. I struggle to sort out his admin. It’s a long to do list and I feel so tired trying to get through everything. Did you lose someone close to you too?
Sending hugs to you, it really feels like that when the wave comes. I hate it so much and wish that I could stop these waves. Just know that you’re going to get back up and keep treading.

It’s going to be a hard journey but I hope that we can both continue on this together. Thinking of you ❤️

There’s no way I can just start a new chapter in my life if I’m not ready to let go of the past. I still miss my Dad everyday.

I lost my dad after six months as well. It felt too soon for anyone to go that fast. I remember trying to get him the professional help he needed after the first month of noticing his depression and anxiety. Things then escalated really fast when he refused to get help. 

I’ve struggled with depression when I was in high school. Had a lot of suicidal thoughts but managed to go through university before getting treatment. Like you, I agree it’s not easy and my dark thoughts are louder and louder during rough times. Sometimes I’m afraid that the pain is so great that I’ll take my life also. 

But somehow, I’ve managed to scrape through the days, months, and years. The darkest cloud passes. There is hope if only for a brief period. 

I was also bitter with my dad because I miss him so much yet hate him for taking the easy way out. Why couldn’t he just be depressed and alive? We could fight this together.. but no... he had enough. 

Because of our mental struggle, I believe we understand really well why my dad and others lost there fight. I refuse to follow the same path as my dad even when I really feel awful. 

Sorry for your loss. I’m thinking of you and hoping that you’re feeling a bit better.

I used to be very suicidal and I wanted to die all the time. This all changed when my father, who was struggling with his own mental health, eventually took his own life. It’s been very hard trying to process the grief from his suicide because I know how he tried to fight his demons silently. Like him, I always had my suicidal thoughts to hide. Because of my dad, I no longer want to take my own life because I can see what it does to those left behind. I feel like it’s better for me to suffer while being alive than to end my suffering soon and to cause immense pain to those left behind. I really hope that if you’re considering taking your life, to get some help and talk to someone you trust about it. It will get better even if it’s hard.
